title: The Man Who Stole the Mona Lisa

sections.name: Hook
lines: ml_hook
In 1911, the most famous painting in the world vanished from the Louvre. And for a whole day, nobody even noticed.
ml_title
This is the theft of the Mona Lisa.

sections.name: The theft
lines: ml_smock
Paris, August 1911. Vincenzo Peruggia, an Italian handyman who had once worked at the Louvre, puts on a white smock, just like the museum's workers.
ml_grab
It's a Monday, when the museum is closed to visitors. He lifts the Mona Lisa off the wall, and carries it to a quiet stairwell.
ml_out
There, he pulls the painting out of its frame, hides it under his smock, and simply walks out of the museum.

sections.name: The empty wall
lines: ml_wall
The next day, a painter comes to sketch her. All he finds are four iron hooks on an empty wall.
ml_crowds
The Louvre closes for a week. When it reopens, crowds line up just to stare at the empty space where she used to hang.

sections.name: The suspects
lines: ml_suspects
Police question suspect after suspect. Even the poet Guillaume Apollinaire is arrested, and a young artist named Pablo Picasso is questioned. Both are innocent.

sections.name: The trunk
lines: ml_trunk
Meanwhile, the Mona Lisa is sitting in a trunk in Peruggia's small Paris room. For more than two years.
ml_florence
In 1913, he takes her to Florence, and offers her to an art dealer. The dealer quietly calls in the director of the Uffizi gallery.
ml_caught
They confirm it's the real thing, and the police arrest Peruggia at his hotel.

sections.name: The ending
lines: ml_home
He said he wanted to return her to Italy. He spent less than a year in prison, and the Mona Lisa went home to the Louvre.
ml_outro
Before the theft, she was just a famous painting. After it, she was the most famous painting in the world. Follow for more true crime, animated.
